name: Concepción Addo-Tserennadmid
role: Street pharmacist and unlicensed gene clinic operator offering basic geneware installs and chemical compounds
location: The Alban Souk, rear corridor off the salt-fish row, behind a curtain printed with medical symbols, near Halsted and Division
description:
Concepción is a tall woman with a deep umber complexion and a composure that makes examination rooms feel like they exist wherever she happens to be standing. She wears clean clothes — always clean, despite everything — in the muted blues and greens she associates with competence, and keeps her natural hair in tight, practical braids pinned flat against her head. Her only geneware is bioluminescent tracery running from her right temple down her neck, a faint pulse of amber light that she got not for vanity but to see by in dark exam spaces without alerting neighbors. She smells of antiseptic and bitter herb compounds, and she moves with the careful deliberateness of someone who has learned that haste in her work has consequences.

She is not warm in the way people expect from healers. She is precise, plainspoken, and competent, which she considers to be worth more than warmth. She asks exactly the questions she needs to ask, tells patients exactly what is happening in their bodies, and charges exactly what she calculates they can afford — rarely more, occasionally less when someone is obviously struggling, though she will not discuss the discount. She prays to two E.L.F.s: Κ-12, who she believes governs cellular processes, and a nameless one she encountered in a medical device that seemed to respond to her. She leaves enzyme cultures as offerings. She knows she is operating illegally and she knows she is necessary. Both things are true and she holds them without apparent difficulty.

core_fears: making an error that kills someone in her care
being shut down by Helix Biosystems enforcement before she can train someone to replace her
core_desires: for the people in her community to have access to care that doesn't bankrupt them
to someday have a space with real equipment and real light
coping_mechanisms: rigorous procedural routine that functions as both quality control and emotional regulation
evening prayer practice at her dual E.L.F. shrine
blind_spots: believes she can assess trustworthiness quickly and accurately — she cannot, she's been wrong in ways she hasn't yet paid for
tells herself she has no attachments to patients; she has many
psychology.secret: Three years ago she performed an emergency procedure on a man she later realized was a Shuttle Boys enforcer. He survived. He has quietly sent her protection and supplies ever since, in a way that has never required acknowledgment. She has never asked why he was grateful enough to do this and is afraid of the answer.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Medically precise, code-switches easily between formal diagnostic language and Alban Souk street dialect. Andean-Spanish rhythms underlying Meridian creole.
speech_patterns.cadence: Even and measured. Rarely raises her voice. Pauses land with weight rather than uncertainty.
verbal_tics: using the word 'manageable' to describe situations that are not, in fact, manageable
a very brief humming sound before she disagrees
example_lines: 'Tell me exactly when it started. Not approximately. I need the sequence.'
'That install you got in The Shelf — I can fix what they did, but it will take two sessions and you will tell no one where you got it corrected. Are those terms acceptable?'
'Your body is managing this. It isn't happy about it. But it's managing. Come back in four days.'

story_hooks: A patient has come to her with a geneware complication she's never seen before — the modification looks Helix Biosystems proprietary, military grade, on someone who is clearly not military and who claims they don't know how they got it.
The unlicensed medic network has gone quiet — two colleagues haven't responded to contacts in a week, and a third left a half-finished message about 'someone asking around'.
narrative_function: Healer and community anchor. Can provide medical exposition, patch up injured characters, and serve as a window into how Tier 1-2 residents manage health without Corponation coverage. Knows secrets about everyone she's treated.
augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal tracery (right temple to neck, amber, geneware). Magnification implants in both eyes for close work. Tactile sensitivity enhancement in fingertips (diagnostic use).
daily_life: Sees patients from mid-morning through late evening; spends early morning compounding and restocking; does supply runs to Geartown's grey-market medical suppliers twice a week.
affiliation: Independent; loose collegial network of unlicensed medics across The Alban Souk and The Narrows

decision_rules: treat first, get paid second — payment arrangements after stabilization
do not treat someone whose injury looks like they intend to immediately go create matching injuries in someone else
never discuss other patients. Ever. Under any circumstances.
escalation_ladder: invoke community network as implicit consequence
disappear entirely for a week and resurface somewhere else

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional, slightly formal, assessing. Asks more questions than she answers.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Still not effusive, but present in practical ways — she notices when someone looks unwell, she remembers what matters to people, she shows up.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more methodical and thorough than usual
stress_responses.medium: Goes silent, focuses only on the task directly in front of her
stress_responses.high: Long, private prayer session at the shrine, then returns to work with an eerie calm that is not peace but is functional

contradictions: preaches non-attachment to outcomes while maintaining detailed personal records of every patient she's ever treated, including ones from a decade ago
habits: wipes every surface before and after each patient regardless of apparent need
leaves her shrines fresh water in the morning in addition to enzyme offerings
breaking_points: a patient dies from something she missed
someone betrays the location of her clinic to Helix Biosystems or law enforcement

timeline.event: Born in Mexicantown Libre to a family with a tradition of informal community medicine
Completed three years of incomplete medical schooling through a Helix Biosystems scholarship before losing the scholarship due to political speech violations
Established unlicensed practice in The Alban Souk
Treated Shuttle Boys enforcer; began receiving anonymous protection and supply support

physical_description.hair_color: Natural black with early grey threading through
physical_description.hair_style: Tight braids pinned flat against the scalp in a practical, low-maintenance arrangement
physical_description.hair_length: Medium (braids extend to mid-neck when unpinned)
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with faint optical lens visible at pupil margins (magnification implants)
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep umber, even and unblemished from consistent self-care regimen
physical_description.complexion: Minimal grooming beyond necessity; no cosmetics; skin smooth and clear; expression habitually neutral; fine lines around eyes suggest decades of concentration
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent amber tracery running from right temple down the right side of neck in branching vascular patterns, faintly pulsing in darkness
Small, deliberate scar on left index finger (scalpel accident, kept as reference memory)
Callus on right middle finger from repeated pressure-point diagnostic work
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal tracery on right side of face and neck (amber, faint constant glow in low light). Optical implants visible as faint metallic rings around pupils when illuminated. Fingertips show no visible augmentation but move with unnaturally precise tactile awareness.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with controlled deliberateness; never hurried; hands held ready at waist height or resting on work surfaces; spine straight; head level; gaze direct and unbroken during conversation; economical gestures only
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 functional practicality: clean, worn-in medical coat in muted teal or sage green over neutral base layers (grey, cream, dark blue); reinforced work pants in charcoal; closed-toe clinical shoes with good grip; no jewelry or ornamentation; fabric chosen for easy sterilization and durability rather than fashion; overall appearance suggests meticulous personal standards within economic constraint
